title: New Windows Service Installation
exclusions: Detects registration of a new Windows service or driver service as Service Control Manager event 7045 in the System channel and, when Audit Security System Extension Success is enabled, security-audit event 4697 in the Security channel. Registration is not proof that the binary executed, the service started, remains installed, is currently running, is malicious, or was created remotely. Event 7045 supplies the SCM service configuration but not the explicit subject/logon fields of 4697; its `UserID` must not be relabelled as the 4697 installing subject. Event 4697 `Subject*` identifies the security context used to install the service, while `ServiceAccount` is the configured future run identity; neither is necessarily a human. The service name is the SCM database key, not necessarily a display name. The recorded image path, type, start type, and account describe creation-time configuration and do not track later `ChangeServiceConfig` or registry edits. Existing-service changes, service starts/stops, package installation without service registration, deletion, binary replacement, current state, authorization, intent, and regulatory attestation are outside scope. Suppression affects notification only; raw 7045/4697 records remain evidence.
evidence: After deployment, retain the effective `[WinEventLog://System]` and `[WinEventLog://Security]` inputs, Audit Security System Extension policy/GPO scope, installed add-on/forwarder versions, host inventory and source-health results, and the version-controlled `windows_new_service_installation_7045_4697` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, triggered actions, and exported result rows. For each finding preserve both raw records when present; `_time`, `_indextime`, recording host/channel, provider, event code, EventRecordID; service name, creation-time image path, service type, start type, and configured service account; 4697 subject name/domain/SID/logon ID; 7045 System-node UserID; source/sourcetype; policy/change/package/driver provenance; binary hash/signature and current SCM configuration collected during response; exception decision; and incident disposition. These artifacts show what Windows reported at registration time. This documentation-only review produced no Windows service, fixture, Splunk result, alert, binary trust, present-state, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated test index and absolute time range, ingest two XML-rendered records for one test service. Record A: `source=XmlWinEventLog:System`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, provider `Service Control Manager`, `EventCode=7045`, `Computer=WIN-APP01`, `ServiceName=Uc127Agent`, `ImagePath=C:\Program Files\UC127\agent.exe --service`, `ServiceType=user mode service`, `StartType=auto start`, `AccountName=LocalSystem`, `UserID=S-1-5-18`, and `EventRecordID=920027`. Record B: `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`, the same sourcetype, provider `Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing`, `EventCode=4697`, `Computer=WIN-APP01`, `ServiceName=Uc127Agent`, `ServiceFileName=C:\Program Files\UC127\agent.exe --service`, `ServiceType=0x10`, `ServiceStartType=2`, `ServiceAccount=LocalSystem`, `SubjectUserName=svc_deploy`, `SubjectDomainName=CONTOSO`, `SubjectUserSid=S-1-5-21-111-222-333-1147`, `SubjectLogonId=0x44ac`, and `EventRecordID=920028`. Expect exactly two rows. Both retain their raw type/start representations; only 4697 populates `install_actor`, actor SID/domain/logon ID, while only 7045 populates `system_user_id`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: In a separate isolated interval, ingest (a) 7045 under `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`, (b) 4697 under `source=XmlWinEventLog:System`, (c) correctly sourced 7045 from provider `Unrelated-Test-Provider`, (d) correctly sourced 4697 from provider `Service Control Manager`, and (e) System 7036 and Security 4698 records with service-like fields. Expect zero rows because source, event, and provider pairs are mandatory and state-transition/scheduled-task events are different semantics. Separately replay a valid SCM 7045 with empty image/account fields and confirm the base report retains one row with `service_image=UNKNOWN` and `service_account=UNKNOWN`; telemetry incompleteness is a review finding, not a reason to lose the registration event.

dataSources: Primary sources are native Windows service-registration events collected continuously from every in-scope host with the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742): Service Control Manager event 7045 from `[WinEventLog://System]` and Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing event 4697 from `[WinEventLog://Security]`. The qualified XML contract is deployment-local `index=wineventlog`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, and `source=XmlWinEventLog:System` or `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`. Event 7045 fields are `ServiceName`, `ImagePath`, `ServiceType`, `StartType`, `AccountName`, `Computer`, System-node `UserID`, and `EventRecordID`. Event 4697 fields are `ServiceName`, `ServiceFileName`, `ServiceType`, `ServiceStartType`, `ServiceAccount`, `SubjectUserSid`, `SubjectUserName`, `SubjectDomainName`, `SubjectLogonId`, `Computer`, and `EventRecordID`. Both require provider identity plus Splunk `_time`, `_indextime`, `host`, `source`, and `sourcetype`. Collection is event-driven Windows Event Log monitoring, not an API, HEC, scripted, or modular-input poll.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742), version 8.1.2 or a later platform-compatible release whose XML source/source-type and 7045/4697 field contracts have been regression-tested locally. Splunkbase listed 10.0.1 as current on 2026-07-28 and compatible with Splunk 9.3/9.4 and 10.x; choose a supported release for the deployed platform instead of assuming the newest package supports older Splunk versions. Deploy input configuration to Windows collection forwarders and parsing/search-time knowledge to the required Splunk tiers. No premium app is required.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" ((source="XmlWinEventLog:System" EventCode=7045) OR (source="XmlWinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4697))
| eval event_code=tonumber(coalesce(EventCode,EventID,event_id)), provider_name=coalesce(Provider_Name,ProviderName,EventSourceName,SourceName,Name), recording_host=coalesce(Computer,ComputerName,dest,host), event_record_id=coalesce(EventRecordID,RecordNumber)
| eval expected_provider=if(event_code=7045,"service control manager","microsoft-windows-security-auditing"), provider_verified=if(lower(provider_name)=expected_provider OR (event_code=7045 AND match(_raw,"(?i)<Provider[^>]+(?:Name|EventSourceName)=['\"]Service Control Manager['\"]")) OR (event_code=4697 AND match(_raw,"(?i)<Provider Name=['\"]Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing['\"]")),1,0)
| where provider_verified=1
| eval provider_name=coalesce(provider_name,if(event_code=7045,"Service Control Manager","Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing")), recording_channel=if(event_code=7045,"System","Security"), service_name=coalesce(ServiceName,"UNKNOWN"), service_image=coalesce(ServiceFileName,ImagePath,"UNKNOWN"), service_type=coalesce(ServiceType,"UNKNOWN"), service_start_type=coalesce(ServiceStartType,StartType,"UNKNOWN"), service_account=coalesce(ServiceAccount,AccountName,"UNKNOWN")
| eval install_actor=if(event_code=4697,coalesce(SubjectUserName,"UNKNOWN"),"NOT_RECORDED_BY_7045"), actor_domain=if(event_code=4697,coalesce(SubjectDomainName,"UNKNOWN"),null()), actor_sid=if(event_code=4697,SubjectUserSid,null()), actor_logon_id=if(event_code=4697,SubjectLogonId,null()), system_user_id=if(event_code=7045,UserID,null()), event_semantics="service_registered_not_proof_of_execution_or_current_state", use_case="UC-1.2.27"
| table _time _indextime recording_host recording_channel event_code provider_name service_name service_image service_type service_start_type service_account install_actor actor_domain actor_sid actor_logon_id system_user_id event_record_id source sourcetype event_semantics use_case
| sort 0 - _time
description: Reports each qualified Windows service registration observed as System event 7045 or Security event 4697 and normalizes their different creation-time field names without merging actor and run-account semantics. It returns all registrations—including drivers and services in standard paths—while explicitly labelling each row as registration evidence rather than proof of execution or current state.
value: A newly registered service or driver can establish durable, privileged execution, but the same mechanism is used by operating-system updates, security tools, and ordinary software. Complete, actor-aware tracking lets security and Windows teams reconcile every registration to an approved deployment, preserve the original binary/configuration evidence, and detect suspicious persistence without hiding services merely because their path looks conventional.
implementation: Enable XML collection for System on every in-scope host and enable Audit Security System Extension Success plus Security collection where actor-rich 4697 is required. Qualify both event/provider/field contracts, then save the SPL as `windows_new_service_installation_7045_4697` and run it every five minutes over a delayed closed window. Retain every base result; route through exact, expiring approval policy after detection. Correlate paired 7045/4697 records, package/change provenance, binary trust, process telemetry, and current SCM configuration before declaring persistence or taking action.
visualization: Lead with host/channel source health and 7045-to-4697 coverage where Security System Extension auditing is expected. Show a newest-first registration table with host, recording channel, event code, service name, creation-time image, type, start type, configured service account, 4697 installing subject, 7045 System UserID, EventRecordID, and raw drilldown. Add 24-hour and 30-day trends by service name, image parent directory, service type/start type, actor, account, and host; panels for driver/boot/system-start registrations, user or network paths, command interpreters, missing fields, and registrations without approved deployment evidence. Do not label a service running or malicious from this dashboard alone.
schema: Native Windows System event 7045 and Security event 4697 service-registration contracts
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable to the authoritative dual-event rule. Current Windows add-on normalization does not guarantee one accelerated CIM dataset containing both provider/channel identities, the 7045 and 4697 event-specific fields, creation-time path/type/start/account, 4697 subject/logon context, 7045 System UserID, and EventRecordID. The previous generic `Change.All_Changes` query could return unrelated changes and lose service-install semantics. Use raw events for detection/evidence; an Endpoint Services inventory is current/sampled configuration, not a substitute for historical registration. Any summary must preserve the full output contract and pass raw parity tests.

knownFalsePositives:
A valid 7045 or 4697 means Windows reported a new SCM registration; it is not a false event because the service is legitimate. False positives arise when a downstream rule labels every registration malicious, treats a conventional path as proof of safety, or opens duplicate incidents for the System/Security pair.

1. **Windows Update, device-driver, or OEM firmware package** — Servicing can register a user-mode service, kernel driver, or file-system driver, including boot/system-start types. Match the exact host, KB/driver package, signed catalog/publisher, service name, image hash, deployment ring, reboot/change window, and package-management record. Suppress notification only for that package/service/hash and bounded rollout; retain driver and early-start registrations for review.

2. **Microsoft Defender temporary `MpKsl*` definition-update drivers** — Defender updates can create randomly suffixed `MpKsl` services under a Defender definition-update path, so a random name or ProgramData path alone is not malicious. Verify Microsoft signature, exact Defender path/version, protection update history, short expected lifetime, and corresponding Defender events. Use an expiring publisher/path/name-pattern policy approved by endpoint security; never allow-list all random driver names or ProgramData.

3. **Microsoft Configuration Manager, Intune, Group Policy software deployment, or MSI installer** — Enterprise deployment systems routinely register product services. Correlate the 4697 subject or 7045 host/time with the named deployment job, package ID, installer process tree, owner, target collection, signed binary, and change. Suppress only the exact package/service/version during its rollout, not the deployment account globally.

4. **EDR, vulnerability scanner, backup, database, monitoring, or remote-management agent install/upgrade** — Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike, Qualys, Nessus, Veeam, SQL tooling, Splunk Universal Forwarder, and similar products can add services and drivers. Confirm vendor signature, approved installer/hash, central-console deployment record, expected service account/start type, and host scope. Maintain exact versioned approval entries with expiry and owner; a familiar vendor name without signature/provenance is insufficient.

5. **PsExec or another approved remote administration/support workflow** — PsExec commonly creates a temporary service such as `PSEXESVC`; remote software tools may do the same. Confirm the originating administrator, support/change ticket, source endpoint, process/network telemetry, expected service name/hash, bounded session, and subsequent cleanup. Suppress only the exact approved session; unexpected remote creation remains high priority.

6. **Application install, upgrade, repair, failover, or cluster-node onboarding** — IIS extensions, database engines, application servers, HA agents, and vendor repair actions can register or replace services. Reconcile service name, image path/arguments, configured account, package version, node role, installer logs, and owner-approved plan. Use host/service/package-specific validity; do not suppress all services under Program Files or Windows.

7. **Golden-image build, disposable lab, automated integration test, or resilience exercise** — Image pipelines and tests may repeatedly register synthetic services. Match build ID, ephemeral asset tag, exact image hash, runner identity, and UTC window. Route to build evidence or use a bounded exception on those assets only; the same registration on production is not covered.

8. **The same installation emits both 7045 and 4697** — This is correlated telemetry, not two independent malicious actions. Match host, service name, image, and near-identical creation time while preserving both EventRecordIDs and event-specific fields. Update one case with the actor-rich 4697 rather than dropping either event or throttling away the Security evidence.

9. **Missing 4697 while 7045 is present** — Usually indicates Audit Security System Extension is disabled, Security collection is absent, or a pipeline gap; it does not make the 7045 benign and does not authorize substituting `UserID` as the installing subject. Route expected-coverage failures to logging owners and investigate the registration with process/change evidence.

**Safe suppression:** keep `windows_new_service_installation_7045_4697` unsuppressed. Apply a downstream `windows_service_install_approvals.csv` requiring exact `recording_host,service_name,service_image,service_account`, approved publisher/hash or package ID, owner, ticket, reason, `valid_from_epoch`, and finite `valid_until_epoch`. Preserve event rows and approval revision. Reject service-name-only, path-only, actor-only, host-wide, wildcard, unsigned/unverified, and non-expiring entries; review driver and boot/system-start approvals separately.
hardware: Supported Microsoft Windows Server and Windows client systems whose local System and, where enabled, Security channels are collected through a qualified direct-forwarder or Windows Event Forwarding topology. The events cover Win32 services and driver services registered with SCM; collector topologies must preserve the originating computer and raw provider/event fields.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary Microsoft event 4697, Audit Security System Extension, Service Control Manager database/configuration, and Microsoft event 7045 guidance plus Splunk Windows Event Log/add-on and Security Content sources and MITRE ATT&CK; no service creation, audit-policy change, fixture replay, add-on deployment, SPL execution, binary verification, current-state query, production validation, Microsoft/Splunk/Windows SME review, or security sign-off

cost.search_load_notes: Sparse 7045/4697 registrations are searched every five minutes over two already-collected Windows channels with exact event/source/provider constraints. License and storage cost belongs primarily to broader System/Security collection; optional downstream binary reputation enrichment has separate cost.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and service-registration contract

Assign Windows platform, endpoint security, software deployment, driver governance, Splunk data/content, incident-response, and evidence owners. Inventory all in-scope Windows hosts and the authoritative change/package systems used to install software. Decide whether each host uses direct Universal Forwarder collection or Windows Event Forwarding, and ensure the topology preserves the originating computer and raw event. Registration monitoring without host inventory and source health can mistake missing telemetry for no service creation.

Install a platform-compatible Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) and qualify the exact add-on, forwarder, Windows, and search-platform combination. Version 8.1.2 is the minimum structured content contract named here; Splunkbase listed 10.0.1 as current at review time but with a newer platform floor. This documentation review did not execute a version matrix, so no `splunkVersions` assertion is made. The search role needs read/schedule permission for `index=wineventlog`; raw Security data, binary reputation, deployment records, and exception writes should be separately restricted. Detection and alert identities do not need service-create, service-control, local administrator, driver-install, registry-write, or software-deployment privileges.

Define the semantics before alerting. Service Control Manager maintains `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services`, with one key per Win32 or driver service. Registration records the SCM service name, binary/driver path and arguments, service type, start type, dependencies and optional run account. Event 7045 is written by **Service Control Manager** to **System** and exposes `ServiceName`, `ImagePath`, `ServiceType`, `StartType`, and `AccountName`; its System-node `UserID` is preserved but is not the explicit installing-subject contract. Event 4697 is written by **Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing** to **Security** when Audit Security System Extension Success is enabled and exposes `Subject*`, `ServiceName`, `ServiceFileName`, `ServiceType`, `ServiceStartType`, and `ServiceAccount`.

Do not confuse identities. The 4697 subject is the account/security context used to install the service. `ServiceAccount`/7045 `AccountName` is the identity configured for the service when it later runs. LocalSystem as a service account is common and not proof that SYSTEM installed it; a SYSTEM subject can represent an installer or management agent and is not automatically benign. Event 7045 alone does not supply the same subject/logon fields. The configured path/account can be changed later without another 7045/4697, and registration does not prove start, execution, persistence success, current state, or maliciousness.

The `wineventlog` index, saved-search name, five-minute schedule/delay, approval lookup, and retention are deployment-owned contracts, not Microsoft or Splunk defaults. Change them consistently in collection, SPL, controls, dashboards, runbooks, and evidence.

## Step 1 — Configure System, Security, and audit-policy collection

Place local input settings in a deployment app or add-on `local/inputs.conf`; never edit `default`. A representative direct-forwarder configuration is:

```ini
[WinEventLog://System]
disabled = 0
start_from = oldest
current_only = 0
checkpointInterval = 5
renderXml = true
index = wineventlog

[WinEventLog://Security]
disabled = 0
start_from = oldest
current_only = 0
checkpointInterval = 5
renderXml = true
index = wineventlog
```

Use GPO to enable **Advanced Audit Policy Configuration > System Audit Policies > System > Audit Security System Extension > Success** on hosts where 4697 actor context is required. Microsoft states this subcategory has no Failure events, so enabling Failure does not add failed-install equivalents. Confirm the effective setting on representative endpoints with `auditpol /get /subcategory:"Security System Extension"` and preserve GPO/resultant-policy evidence. Event 7045 in System is the broader SCM source; 4697 availability depends on supported OS/audit policy and Security collection. Do not disable 7045 monitoring merely because 4697 is expected.

Splunk's qualified XML contract is `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog` with `source=XmlWinEventLog:System` or `XmlWinEventLog:Security`. Classic rendering and historical channel-suffixed source types use different fields. Verify `renderXml` and effective input precedence with `splunk btool inputs list WinEventLog://System --debug` and the Security equivalent. Distribute add-on parsing/search knowledge to the tiers required by the deployment. For WEF, validate originating `Computer`/host and avoid duplicate local-plus-forwarded ownership.

Collection is event-driven: there is no API poll interval. A successful registration normally creates one 7045; a qualified host with Success auditing can also produce 4697, but do not demand perfect pairing until the exact OS, policy, collection, and timing paths are tested. Event volume is low and proportional to service/driver registrations, while ingest cost is dominated by broader System/Security channels. Preserve enough local log capacity for forwarding outages.

After deployment, run a source-health search over all expected hosts and inspect sanitized or approved live 7045/4697 records. Require provider, source, EventCode, Computer, EventRecordID, service name, path, type, start type, account, and 4697 subject fields. Keep raw representations: 7045 commonly renders descriptive type/start text while 4697 documents numeric/hex values. Do not force them into one label without a tested mapping. Report 7045-without-4697 rates only for hosts where policy and Security collection are independently confirmed.

## Step 2 — Create, understand, schedule, and route the search

Save the catalogue SPL as `windows_new_service_installation_7045_4697`. Schedule it at `*/5 * * * *` over a closed delayed window such as `earliest=-10m@m latest=-5m@m`. Measure p95/p99 indexing delay and move the window or add a keyed late-arrival recovery process if ordinary lag exceeds five minutes. Keep time modifiers in saved-search configuration so the catalogue query remains reusable.

### Understanding this SPL

The first clause accepts only System 7045 and Security 4697 under the generic XML sourcetype. Provider validation then requires Service Control Manager for 7045 and Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing for 4697, with a narrow raw-XML fallback when the installed add-on does not expose a provider field. This blocks same-number events from unrelated providers and swapped-channel fixtures. Recording host and EventRecordID are retained for evidence.

Normalization is event-specific rather than fictional. `service_image` prefers 4697 `ServiceFileName` then 7045 `ImagePath`; start type prefers `ServiceStartType` then `StartType`; configured account prefers `ServiceAccount` then `AccountName`. Type/start strings remain exactly as extracted because one event can be numeric and the other rendered text. Only 4697 populates installing actor/domain/SID/logon ID. Only 7045 populates `system_user_id`. Missing service configuration becomes `UNKNOWN`, and the valid registration row remains visible. Every output states `service_registered_not_proof_of_execution_or_current_state`.

One raw event produces one row. When both events represent the same installation, correlate host, service name, image, and a narrow time interval in the case-management layer while preserving both rows and EventRecordIDs. Do not `dedup` on service name: reinstallations, rapid replacement, differing images, and separate hosts are meaningful. Do not throttle 7045 so aggressively that later actor-rich 4697 is discarded; update the same case or group notifications after a short correlation delay.

Trigger tracking on every row. Apply urgency downstream: driver types/boot/system start; user-writable, temporary, network, or command-interpreter paths; unsigned/untrusted binaries; unexpected service accounts; high-value hosts; absent package/change provenance; suspicious installing subjects; and remote-execution context are higher risk. Standard Windows or Program Files paths reduce neither registration truth nor adversary possibility. Microsoft recommends path/type/start/account review, but those are triage dimensions rather than a safe base-filter allowlist.

Keep the base report unsuppressed. Apply `windows_service_install_approvals.csv` only after detection with exact host, service, image, account, trusted package/publisher/hash, owner/ticket, and finite epochs. Record approval revision and match status. Never auto-delete a service, kill a process, remove a driver, modify registry configuration, disable an account, or isolate/reboot a host from a registration event alone.

## Step 3 — Validate event semantics, completeness, and controls

Run the positive and negative `controlTest` scenarios in an isolated index with absolute times. Assert two positive rows and every field. Confirm the 7045 row uses ImagePath/StartType/AccountName, preserves UserID, and says its actor is not recorded by 7045. Confirm the 4697 row uses ServiceFileName/ServiceStartType/ServiceAccount and preserves the distinct installing subject. Swapped sources, wrong providers, 7036 service state, and 4698 scheduled-task creation must return zero. A valid 7045 missing configuration must remain visible with UNKNOWN values.

Generate safe live evidence only on a disposable lab host. Register a benign, signed test service through a reviewed installer or `sc.exe create`, without pointing to a production binary or privileged network path. Compare **Event Viewer > Windows Logs > System** 7045 and **Event Viewer > Windows Logs > Security** 4697 with Splunk. Match UTC time, computer, providers, event IDs/record IDs, service key name, image including arguments, raw type/start values, configured account, and 4697 subject/logon. Remove the test service through the approved rollback after preserving evidence; remember deletion does not erase the historical registration.

Use `sc.exe qc <service-name>`, `Get-CimInstance Win32_Service`, `QueryServiceConfig`, or Services.msc to compare current configuration, but label it as a later observation. Then deliberately change image path, account, or start type in the lab and prove the original event remains creation-time history rather than current configuration. Start and stop the test to prove 7045/4697 do not themselves establish execution or present running state.

Validate at least two OS roles and the exact add-on release. Test user-mode own/share services, kernel/file-system drivers, automatic/manual/disabled start, LocalSystem and named accounts, quoted paths with arguments, environment variables, UNC paths, non-English rendering, blank driver account, local/domain/SYSTEM installing subjects, event delay, checkpoint restart, WEF host attribution, and duplicate routes. Compare bounded Event Viewer/Get-WinEvent counts with Splunk. Do not assume one-to-one 7045/4697 until audit policy and both channels are known complete.

Maintain independent source health: expected hosts versus recent System/Security counts, forwarder phone-home, queue lag, input state, policy state, and duplicate `(Computer,Channel,EventRecordID)`. A host with no new services can be healthy; 7045/4697 absence is not a heartbeat. Track parser changes after add-on upgrades and rerun controls before production acceptance.

## Step 4 — Operationalize triage, dashboards, approvals, and evidence

Build the dashboard in `visualization` with source health first. Restrict raw Security and binary/path data to appropriate operations/security roles and limit approval lookup writes to governed owners. Keep creation-time event data separate from current configuration and process execution. Add a case correlation that links paired 7045/4697 without suppressing either raw event.

The response runbook should: (1) verify source/event/provider and raw identity; (2) distinguish service key name from display name; (3) identify Win32 versus driver and start type; (4) separate 4697 installing subject from configured service account and 7045 UserID; (5) inspect current SCM configuration and `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<name>` read-only; (6) acquire the binary safely, resolve environment variables/arguments, and verify path, hash, signature, catalog, publisher, creation time, and prevalence; (7) correlate installer/process/EDR, 4624 logon, network, remote-service, package, update, driver, GPO, deployment, and change telemetry; (8) determine whether it started and its impact using independent process/service events; (9) check other hosts for the same service/hash; and (10) document authorization and disposition.

A confirmed adversarial registration can support MITRE ATT&CK T1543.003. Do not map every legitimate registration to malicious persistence, and do not claim T1569.002 Service Execution unless independent evidence shows execution. A service in Windows/System32 can still be malicious; a service outside Program Files can be legitimate. Signature, package provenance, actor/process context, host role, and current behavior decide priority.

For containment, coordinate with Windows, application, and incident owners. Preserve the binary, registry/service configuration, raw events, process memory/logs, network context, and dependent-service impact before deletion or reboot. Drivers and boot/system-start services can affect startup; removing a legitimate or malicious driver incorrectly can make a host unbootable. Never issue `sc delete`, remove a registry key/file, change service account, disable endpoint protection, or reboot solely from this alert.

Retain the artifacts named in `evidence` under local incident/audit policy. The cost profile's 90 days is advisory, not a legal requirement. This documentation can specify repeatable evidence but cannot prove complete source coverage, present configuration, binary safety, authorization, execution, persistence success, or compliance.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot without corrupting service semantics

- **7045 appears but 4697 does not:** verify effective Audit Security System Extension Success, Security input, source metadata, local Security log, forwarding, and search time. 7045 remains valid registration evidence; do not copy UserID into the missing 4697 subject.
- **4697 appears but 7045 does not:** inspect local System 7045, `[WinEventLog://System]`, provider/source filters, channel retention, WEF subscription, checkpoint, and time bounds. Keep the actor-rich event and report System coverage loss.
- **Events arrive as `WinEventLog:System`/`Security` or channel-suffixed sourcetypes:** identify Classic/historical rendering and its real field contract. Migrate or implement a separately tested compatibility branch; do not call channel-specific source names current XML sourcetypes.
- **Provider is null or wrong:** compare raw XML, add-on search-time knowledge, and effective props. Restore precise provider extraction or the narrow raw fallback; do not remove provider validation globally.
- **Service name is confused with display name:** use `ServiceName` as the SCM key from the registration event and query current display name separately. Do not join approvals only on mutable/localized display labels.
- **Actor equals LocalSystem but service account is a domain user, or vice versa:** expected distinction. Subject is installation context; service account is configured run identity. Preserve both and investigate separately.
- **7045/4697 type or start values disagree in format:** one can be rendered text and the other numeric/hex. Preserve raw values and use a versioned mapping only after fixtures prove equivalence; do not treat formatting as two installations.
- **Image path is empty, truncated, quoted, or contains arguments/environment variables:** preserve raw data, inspect XML and current QueryServiceConfig, resolve variables without executing the command, and validate add-on parsing. Keep incomplete rows visible.
- **Duplicate pages for one installation:** correlate host/service/image/time and update one case while preserving both channels/EventRecordIDs. Check WEF plus local duplication before calling every duplicate a 7045/4697 pair.
- **Dashboard says service is running:** remove that claim. Query current state or process telemetry independently; registration events are historical configuration observations.
- **Approval lookup hides an unexpected binary:** verify exact-key joins, duplicate rows, epochs, hash/publisher/package requirements, and ACLs. Reject broad service/path/actor allowlists and preserve suppressed matches.
- **High alert volume after patching or agent rollout:** correlate exact package/change rings and apply finite versioned approvals. Do not disable base collection or filter all services under Windows, Program Files, ProgramData, SYSTEM, or a deployment account.
grandmaExplanation: We record when Windows adds a new background service or driver, what program it is set to use, and who installed it when Windows provides that detail. The team then checks whether it belongs to an approved update or could give an intruder a hidden way to keep control.
